items.summary: Slip Op. 25-110, dated August 22, 2025, in Citribel N.V. v. United States (Court No. 24-00010), is an opinion by Judge M. Miller Baker of the U.S. Court of International Trade. It remands to the Department of Commerce for reconsideration of its calculation of Citribel's costs of production in the administrative review of the antidumping duty order on citric acid from Belgium, where Citribel contested the use of annualized rather than quarterly conversion costs. The court also declines to redact certain record material that it finds does not qualify as business proprietary information under 19 C.F.R. § 351.105(c).

items.summary: Slip Op. 24-53, dated May 1, 2024, is a Court of International Trade opinion and order by Judge Claire R. Kelly addressing consolidated motions for judgment on the agency record concerning the Department of Commerce's final determination in the 2019-2020 administrative review of the antidumping duty order on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells from the People's Republic of China. The plaintiffs challenge 12 determinations, including Commerce's selection of Romanian HTS 7007.19.80 data to value solar glass, its valuation of ocean and air freight, its calculation of surrogate financial ratios, and its application of adverse facts available. The bracketed summary states that the court sustains in part and remands in part Commerce's determination, and the text provided is truncated before the court's final holdings.

items.summary: Slip Op. 25-67, dated May 30, 2025 and filed June 6, 2025, is a Court of International Trade opinion and order by Judge Claire R. Kelly reviewing Commerce's redetermination on remand in the eighth administrative review of the antidumping duty order on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells from China. The court sustains Commerce's use of Freightos data to value air freight and remands Commerce's selection of Romanian HTS 7007.19.80 data to value solar glass and its calculation of an adverse inference using facts otherwise available. The opinion notes that plaintiffs challenged Commerce's decision to make no changes following the court's earlier remand order.

Kelly reviewing Commerce's Final Results of Redetermination Pursuant to Court Remand, filed September 26, 2025, in the 2019-20 administrative review of the antidumping duty order on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells from China. The bracketed summary states that the court sustains in part and remands in part Commerce's redetermination. The background recounts that the court's earlier decision in Jinko II had sustained the air freight valuation and remanded the solar glass valuation and the adverse inference methodology, and the text provided is truncated before the court's holdings on the second remand.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the District of Kansas's grant of summary judgment to Cozy Inn and Stephen Howard on First Amendment claims against the City of Salina, Kansas, concerning the city's sign code and its handling of a sign permit application for a painted wall display. The opinion explains that the sign code requires permits for signs, while murals are not regulated, and that the city placed the permit application on hold in February 2024. The plaintiffs had sought a declaration that the sign code and its enforcement are a content-based restriction on speech and an unlawful prior restraint. The court exercised jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1291 and affirmed.

items.summary: In this unpublished per curiam opinion, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the convictions and 480-month total sentence of Alex Winters for possession of a firearm as a felon, possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime. The court held, under plain-error review, that Winters did not show a double jeopardy violation from consecutive sentences on the drug offense and the § 924(c) count, relying on circuit precedent. The opinion also addresses Winters's challenge, raised for the first time on appeal, to the application of the career-offender enhancement under the Sentencing Guidelines.
